owner_request: Check the old thread that it's still working under old rules and maybe there's more to improve build times
standing_goal: Drastically reduce build/validation work without sacrificing features or relevant checks.
confirmed_findings: The old combined-validation and asset threads loaded mandatory STE sources before the shared plain-writing update. Root sent the active owners the changed writing/task paths and instructed them not to repeat completed validation.
Each of smc_reachability_test.sh, smc_drum_mutes_test.sh, smc_performance_abort_test.sh and ui_feedback_test.sh calls host/build_host.sh with X0X_HOST_OUT pointing at a temporary host binary.
None of those four scripts runs or otherwise reads that temporary simulator binary. Each separately compiles and runs its own C probe, which includes host/x0x_host.c directly.

The useful setup from host/build_host.sh is its generated headers. A generate-only mode can stop before the unused -O2 full simulator compile while retaining original asset generation and test probe flags/assertions.
tests/run_tests.sh retains an explicit host-build test and actual simulator scenarios. Removing the four discarded auxiliary binaries does not remove that coverage.

tools/quickcheck.sh still performs an Elite target build before selecting tests for all ordinary changes, including host/web-only changes. Its fallback also runs a fixed firmware-oriented test set when few tests match. Narrow automatic routing needs a separate checked change; do not simply delete the fallback.

quickcheck also invokes approximate STE checks by default despite the new writing default. No dictionary is involved, but this is additional obsolete routine work to assess in a later scoped checker change.

The current asset cache owner measured 33.63 s cold / 21.82 s warm initially and found warm lookup recompiles the break renderer. It is already replacing that with a dependency probe. Root will not duplicate it.
recommended_implementation: Add a clearly named generate-only option to host/build_host.sh. Preserve its default full-simulator behavior and existing flags/environment.
Use this option in the four scripts. Leave probe C files, assertions, compile options and pass/fail criteria unchanged.
Keep setup failures fatal and preserve clean-temp startup and cleanup. Check empty generated-header startup, custom break-bank behavior and default full-host invocation with controlled fixtures.

Run the four real probes once in the supported host environment, preserving their relevant configuration. Record timers and exact command scopes. Do not rebuild firmware/controller or run a full suite for a host setup-only change.
Use existing checked baseline logs where inputs match; do not run four expensive old simulator builds solely to reproduce a timing baseline.

The asset lane owns tools/build.py, tools/asset_cache.py, its tests and asset docs. Do not edit its live files. A later checked combination can route host generation through the same cache; report repeated break generation as a remaining limit if it persists.
limits: No implementation, runtime-saving, target-build or device PASS is claimed by this audit.
Quickcheck routing/STE-default changes are findings only and are not part of the four-helper implementation.
